description:
## Context

`OctoPi.AI.SanitizeUnicode` (`apps/octo_pi_ai/lib/octo_pi/ai/sanitize_unicode.ex`) is fully implemented and tested (5 passing tests). It strips invalid UTF-8 byte sequences from binaries before they are embedded in JSON sent to provider APIs. It is completely unwired — no caller exists in the codebase.

Upstream (`tmp/pi-mono/packages/ai/src/utils/sanitize-unicode.ts`) calls `sanitizeSurrogates()` at request-serialization time (not at message construction), applied to every text string before it enters the JSON payload.

## Upstream call sites

**Anthropic** (`tmp/pi-mono/packages/ai/src/anthropic.ts`):
- System prompt text (lines 838, 847)
- User message strings and text blocks (lines 936, 944)
- Assistant text blocks, thinking, and thinking signature (lines 977, 995, 1000)

**OpenAI** (`tmp/pi-mono/packages/ai/src/openai-completions.ts`, `openai-responses-shared.ts`):
- System message content (line 710 / 130)
- User message content and text items (lines 730, 737 / 140, 147)
- Assistant output text blocks (lines 768, 780 / 189, 233, 249)

## Implementation steps

### 1. Anthropic provider
**File:** `apps/octo_pi_ai_anthropic/lib/octo_pi/ai/providers/anthropic/request.ex`

Add `alias OctoPi.AI.SanitizeUnicode` at the top. Read the file to find the exact function/line numbers, then wrap text at these 6 logical points:

a. System prompt — non-OAuth (in `system_field/2` or equivalent, ~line 195):
```elixir
[%{"type" => "text", "text" => SanitizeUnicode.sanitize(prompt)}]
```
b. System prompt — OAuth user prompt (~line 203): same pattern
c. User message string (in `user_block/1` or `convert_user_content/1`, ~line 272)
d. User message text block (~line 277)
e. Assistant text block (in `assistant_block/2`, ~line 287)
f. Assistant thinking block (~line 296): wrap `block.thinking`

Tool result content is already covered because it routes through `user_block/1`.

### 2. OpenAI provider
**File:** `apps/octo_pi_ai_openai/lib/octo_pi/ai/providers/openai/request.ex`

Add alias, then wrap at ~5 locations:
a. System message content (in system messages builder, ~line 366)
b. Developer role content (~line 363)
c. User message string (in `convert_user/1`, ~line 421)
d. User message text part (in `user_content_part/1`, ~line 430)
e. Assistant text content (in `convert_assistant/2` — find text block extraction)

Do NOT sanitize: tool call arguments (JSON dicts), image content (binary), internal synthetic bridge messages.

### 3. Docstring update

Update the module docstring in `apps/octo_pi_ai/lib/octo_pi/ai/sanitize_unicode.ex` to clarify:
- Elixir handles invalid UTF-8 bytes (not UTF-16 surrogates as in TypeScript)
- The implementation is semantically equivalent — both prevent JSON serialization errors
- Applied at request-serialization time only, not during message construction

### 4. Tests

Add integration-level tests verifying:
- Anthropic request with user message containing invalid UTF-8 bytes serializes cleanly
- OpenAI request with system prompt containing invalid UTF-8 bytes serializes cleanly
- Valid unicode (emoji, CJK, multibyte) passes through unchanged

Existing unit tests in `apps/octo_pi_ai/test/sanitize_unicode_test.exs` — do not modify.

## Notes
- Read both `request.ex` files before editing — line numbers above are approximate.
- Do NOT add sanitization inside decoders — streaming responses from provider-controlled streams are already valid UTF-8.
title: Wire OctoPi.AI.SanitizeUnicode into Anthropic and OpenAI request builders
